title: Free a hard drive from its tool-less carrier while holding one sprung rail open
instruction: Take the hard drive out of its carrier and put it on the anti-static mat.
context: Computer repairers and computer support specialists (O*NET 49-2011.00, 15-1232.00) take drives out of desktop computers to replace, test or recover them. In many desktops the drive sits in a tool-less plastic carrier whose two side rails each hold two pins in the drive's screw holes. Dell's service manual for its OptiPlex 5060 Tower says to "Pull one side of the drive bracket to disengage the pins", then lift the drive out, and drive-handling rules (Lenovo) say "Do not bump drives". The instruction only says to take the drive out and put it on the mat. Each rail is sprung inward and springs back into the holes as soon as it is let go, so one hand holds a rail out while the other lifts that side of the drive, which pivots on the other rail's pins, slides it off those pins and lifts it clear. Pulled straight up with both rails in place, the drive is held by the pins and a rail breaks.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A 2.5-inch hard drive (10.02 x 6.985 x 0.95 cm, 115 g, a label on its top cover) lies label up in a tool-less carrier, its middle at x 26, y 4, its front end toward the arms. The carrier's dark base (x 18.4 to 31.6, y 0.9 to 7.1, 1.2 cm tall) is fixed to the table. Its two blue rails (20 g each) run along the drive's sides, each hinged 0.7 cm below the drive and sprung inward; each has two pins standing in the drive's side screw holes (at x 22.4 and 30.05, 0.3 cm above the drive's bottom) and a tab standing 8 cm tall at its front end (x 19.4 to 20.7, in front of the drive). A grey-blue anti-static mat (20 x 15 cm, 2 mm thick) is fixed on the table at x 16 to 36, y -24 to -9. The drive is loose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The bodies' poses are read from the simulation, and each gripper's centre from the arm's joints. The drive counts as dropped or knocked once its middle moves down faster than 0.5 m/s (as after a free fall of 1.3 cm) or its speed changes by more than 0.6 m/s within one 50 ms control step; a rail counts as broken once its hinge has given way (its joint breaks under 10 N or 0.5 N m, as when the drive is pulled up against the pins or the rail is forced past 40 degrees open). Either sets the score to 0 for the rest of the run. Otherwise partial credit is the best stage reached: 0.25 one side of the drive lifted off its rail's pins (that side's two holes off the pins and risen 4 mm or more); 0.5 the drive out of the carrier (all four holes off the pins, and its lowest point 1 cm or more above the carrier's base or its middle 6 cm or more from where it started); 0.75 the drive lying on the mat (label up, tilted 10 degrees or less, its middle over the mat at least 5 mm in from its edges, its lowest point within 4 mm of the mat's top), at rest, not held (no gripper's centre within 7 cm of the drive's middle and keeping the same offset to it). 1.0: that, with both rails back home (within 2 degrees of shut) and both grippers 6 cm or more from the drive and from the rails' tabs, still for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. With a real carrier, a drop or knock and a broken rail are judged from the overhead and wrist videos, and the stages with a ruler on the overhead photo.
reset_notes: Put the drive back in the carrier, label up and front end toward the arms, with all four pins in its side holes and both rails shut, and clear the mat, as in the screenshot. In the simulation each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim 6.1 (PhysX), 20 Hz control. The drive is a rigid box with four 4 mm square side holes (its real M3 holes are 3 mm across). Each plastic rail's flex is a hinge 7 mm below the drive on a spring (0.2 N m/rad); its joint breaks under 10 N or 0.5 N m. The rails' tabs stand 8 cm tall so that a gripper can push one. The carrier's base is fixed to the table. A drop or knock is judged from the drive's speed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers went to the drive in its carrier and pressed and pulled at it and at the rails; a rail was forced out flat past its stop and broke off, and the drive stayed in the carrier); demo: 1.0
